name: brogue
why: A classic roguelike with a famously deep, emergent design that rewards long, careful play sessions.

brief.what_it_is: Brogue is a single-player roguelike in which you descend a randomly generated dungeon to retrieve the Amulet of Yendor from the 26th floor and bring it back to the surface. You play through the keyboard (vi-keys hjklyubn or keypad) or the mouse, and a help screen opens with ? or the Menu button. The README says the dungeon is full of monsters, traps and items, and that survival depends on using what you find. The original game is by Brian Walker, and Brogue: Community Edition (CE) is the continuation the homepage now points players to.
brief.why_it_exists: The original site frames the game as a challenge with a single goal and a lot of danger: "Your goal is to travel to the 26th subterranean floor of the dungeon, retrieve the Amulet of Yendor and return with it to the surface." CE exists to "fix bugs and crashes", add quality-of-life features, and keep gameplay exciting.
brief.how_it_works: Each game generates a new dungeon, and character progress comes from items rather than experience points. The original README says experience was removed "to reward exploration instead of combat". Scrolls of Enchantment permanently improve one item, and staffs recharge over time. Allies can be freed from monsters that have captured them, and gold only sets the final score.

brief.install_notes: Linux: the CE README says to install SDL2 and SDL2_image first. Debian/Ubuntu: libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-image-2.0-0. Fedora: SDL2 SDL2_image. Arch: sdl2 sdl2_image. Mac: the app is unsigned, so the first run needs right-click then Open. Graphical tiles are included and toggled with G. Building from source needs BUILD.md, which I did not read. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: The original site lists an unusual set of systems: searching takes five turns in a row, stealth is a visible range, allies are won by freeing captives, and enchantment scrolls are described as indispensable and unique to Brogue. Its item and weapon designs, such as whips that reach five spaces and flails that strike when you step between adjacent cells, are more specific than most roguelikes.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell. The homepage tells players to use Brogue: Community Edition for the current version, and the CE GitHub README describes an active project with a benevolent-dictator model, contribution guide, and Discord and IRC channels. I did not find a release date or last-commit date, so the exact activity level is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes v1.7.5, which is an older release. The CE README warns that CE "may differ" from the wiki. I could not confirm which version the Homebrew formula installs. Linux needs SDL2 libraries installed separately. The Mac app is unsigned. The original site's license note says AGPLv3 for later versions. The original 1.7.5 homepage is long and was cut off at 40000 characters, so I did not read every item note.

judge.reason: Brogue is a standout roguelike whose item-driven progression and tightly interacting dungeon systems make each run a compact lesson in emergent tactics.

entry.title: Brogue
entry.tldr: A roguelike with no experience points: descend 26 randomly generated floors to fetch the Amulet of Yendor, surviving on what you find and how you use it.
entry.deeper_look:
Brogue is a single-player dungeon crawler. Each run generates a new dungeon, and your goal is to reach the 26th floor, take the Amulet of Yendor, and carry it back to the surface. You play with vi-keys (hjklyubn), the keypad, or the mouse. The `?` key opens a help screen.

The design choice that sets it apart is that your character does not level up. The original README says experience was removed "to reward exploration instead of combat". Power comes from items. Scrolls of Enchantment permanently improve one item of your choosing, staffs recharge over time, and allies can be won by freeing captives from the monsters holding them. Gold has no use except to set your score at death or victory.

The original game is by Brian Walker. The homepage now points players to Brogue: Community Edition (CE), a continuation that exists to "fix bugs and crashes", add quality-of-life features, and keep the game exciting. The idea underneath is that a game with few systems, all interacting, can be deep enough to replay for years. Every choice about where to put your enchantments shapes the whole run.
entry.install:
brew install brogue
# pulls in sdl2-compat and sdl2_image; graphical tiles are included and toggled with G

entry.whats_unique: Character growth comes entirely from items rather than experience, and the item designs are unusually specific. Whips reach five spaces, flails strike as you step between adjacent cells, and searching takes five turns in a row.
entry.caveats: The original homepage describes the older v1.7.5, the CE README warns CE "may differ" from the wiki, and I could not confirm which version Homebrew installs.
